BonaLabs: external Telegram scheduling
=====================================

Status: configuration prepared; external account setup and verification pending.

Use cron-job.org to request the existing workflow every 15 minutes. The service
is free according to its FAQ, checked October 23, 2026. No new Telegram bot or
webhook is needed. This removes reliance on GitHub's cron scheduler, but runner
queues, service outages and deployment time can still delay visible updates.

1. Create a free account at https://console.cron-job.org/signup and verify it.

2. Create a dedicated GitHub fine-grained personal access token:
   https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
   Name: BonaLabs news scheduler
   Resource owner: BonaLabs
   Repository access: Only select repositories > bonalabs.github.io
   Repository permissions: Actions > Read and write
   Leave other optional permissions unset. GitHub includes Metadata read access.
   Choose an expiry and remember to renew it before that date. If organization
   approval is required, wait until the token is approved before testing.

   Store this token only in the scheduler's Authorization header below. Do not
   paste it into chat, a repository file or the request URL. Actions write access
   also permits managing runs in this repository; it is not scoped to one
   workflow. The scheduler does not need the Telegram bot token.

3. Create one cron job in https://console.cron-job.org/ with these settings:

   Title: BonaLabs Telegram news
   URL: https://api.github.com/repos/BonaLabs/bonalabs.github.io/actions/workflows/telegram-news.yml/dispatches
   Schedule: every 15 minutes, all hours and days
   Timezone: America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires
   Request method: POST
   Request body: {"ref":"main"}

   Add these request headers in the advanced settings:
   Accept: application/vnd.github+json
   Content-Type: application/json
   X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10
   Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN

   Replace YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN in the service's form, keeping the space after
   Bearer. Enable failure and automatic-disable notifications, then save and
   enable the job. The existing workflow already accepts workflow_dispatch;
   no workflow code change is required for this request.

4. Test the job once. A successful API response only means GitHub accepted the
   dispatch. Open Actions and verify that BOTH build and deploy finish green:
   https://github.com/BonaLabs/bonalabs.github.io/actions/workflows/telegram-news.yml

   Then allow two scheduled intervals without pressing Run workflow. Check the
   cron-job.org history and corresponding GitHub runs. External triggers appear
   as workflow_dispatch, not schedule. Confirm the next normal Telegram post
   reaches https://bonalabs.net/ after a successful deployment.
   A homepage left open checks the published snapshot every five minutes;
   refreshing the page requests it immediately. The snapshot's updated_at only
   changes when its posts change, so it is not a record of every successful poll.

5. Keep the existing GitHub cron during setup. Its concurrency group serializes
   workflow runs, so both triggers use the same bot consumer. Once the external
   schedule is verified, the native cron can be reduced to a less frequent
   fallback. Do not run a second bot consumer or install a Telegram webhook.

Troubleshooting:
- 401: check the token or its expiry.
- 403/404: check token owner, repository selection, Actions write permission,
  organization approval and the exact workflow URL.
- 422: check the JSON body and ref main.
- Accepted request but skipped build: check TELEGRAM_FEED_ENABLED=true in the
  GitHub repository's Actions variables.
- Accepted request but failed workflow: inspect its failed step in Actions.
  Scheduler success alone does not verify collection or deployment.
- To stop external scheduling, disable this cron job and revoke its dedicated
  token in GitHub. Existing native scheduled and manual runs remain available.

References:
https://cron-job.org/en/faq/
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event
